title: Transmission Friction Element "A" Apply Time Range/Performance
plain: One of the clutches or bands inside the automatic transmission (element A) is taking longer or shorter than expected to apply during a shift.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission light on
Slipping, flare or harsh shifts
Delayed engagement into gear

causes.name: Low, dirty or wrong transmission fluid
Worn clutch pack or band
Sticking pressure control solenoid or valve body
Internal fluid leak from worn seals
Transmission adaptive values need to be reset or relearned

checks: Check the transmission fluid level and condition
Look for related solenoid or pressure codes
Have a shop check line pressure and shift data
fix: Start with the fluid and any solenoid faults; worn clutches may need a transmission repair or rebuild.

title: Shift Solenoid "F"
plain: The computer is watching the shift solenoid "F" and has spotted an electrical fault. This solenoid inside the automatic transmission directs fluid to change gears.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh, late or erratic shifts
Transmission may go into limp mode (stuck in one gear)

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the shift solenoid "F"
Broken or chafed wire in the shift solenoid "F" circuit
Failed shift solenoid "F"
Blown fuse or failed relay feeding the circuit
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the shift solenoid "F", checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and resistance of the part with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the shift solenoid "F".

title: Shift Solenoid "F" Performance/Stuck Off
plain: The shift solenoid "F" is not responding the way the computer expects. This solenoid inside the automatic transmission directs fluid to change gears.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh, late or erratic shifts
Transmission may go into limp mode (stuck in one gear)

causes.name: Sticking shift solenoid "F"
Low, dirty or wrong transmission fluid
Worn valve body or internal fluid leak
Worn clutches inside the transmission

checks: Check the transmission fluid level and condition
Look for other transmission codes
Have the solenoid tested and commanded with a scan tool
fix: Service the fluid if it is low or dirty; if the code returns, replace the shift solenoid or valve body.

title: Shift Solenoid "F" Intermittent
plain: The computer is watching the shift solenoid "F" and is seeing a signal that cuts in and out. This solenoid inside the automatic transmission directs fluid to change gears.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on

Transmission may go into limp mode (stuck in one gear)

causes.name: Loose connector or chafed wire that loses contact over bumps
Shift solenoid "F" failing on and off
Corrosion inside the connector
Poor ground connection

checks: Wiggle the wiring for the shift solenoid "F" with the engine running while watching live data
Check connector pins for corrosion or spread terminals
Note when it happens (hot, cold, bumps) to narrow it down
fix: Repair the loose or corroded connection; replace the shift solenoid "F" if the wiring is solid.

title: Unexpected Mechanical Gear Disengagement
plain: The transmission dropped out of gear when it was not supposed to, as if it briefly went into neutral.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission light on
Engine revs up suddenly while driving
Loss of drive or a bump when gear re-engages

causes.name: Low transmission fluid
Worn clutches slipping inside the transmission
Sticking solenoid or valve body
Worn shift linkage or detent
Transmission computer software issue

checks: Check the fluid level and condition
Look for other transmission codes
Check for software updates for the transmission computer
fix: Fix the fluid level or the faulty solenoid; internal wear may need a rebuild.

title: Hydraulic Power Unit Leakage
plain: The hydraulic unit that operates an automated or dual-clutch transmission is losing pressure, as if it has a leak.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission light on
Slow or failed gear changes
Car may not move or may not select a gear

causes.name: Fluid leak from the hydraulic unit or lines
Worn hydraulic pump or accumulator
Low hydraulic fluid
Faulty pressure sensor

checks: Check the hydraulic fluid level and look for leaks
Check system pressure with a scan tool
fix: Repair the leak or replace the hydraulic unit or accumulator.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid "D" Control Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The computer is watching the pressure control solenoid "D" control circuit and is getting a signal that does not make sense for current conditions. This solenoid inside the automatic transmission sets the fluid pressure that applies the clutches during shifts.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh, late or erratic shifts
Transmission may go into limp mode (stuck in one gear)

causes.name: Failing or sticking pressure control solenoid "D"
Low, dirty or wrong transmission fluid
Wiring or connector with high resistance
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the pressure control solenoid "D" control circuit reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Find out whether the pressure control solenoid "D" itself or the system it works with is at fault, then repair or replace as needed.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid "D" Control Circuit Low
plain: The computer is watching the pressure control solenoid "D" control circuit and is reading a voltage that is lower than it should be, which often means a short to ground or a failed part. This solenoid inside the automatic transmission sets the fluid pressure that applies the clutches during shifts.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh, late or erratic shifts
Transmission may go into limp mode (stuck in one gear)

causes.name: Control wire to the pressure control solenoid "D" shorted to ground
Failed pressure control solenoid "D"
Corroded or loose connector
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the wiring in the pressure control solenoid "D" control circuit for rubbed-through insulation touching metal
Check the wiring for a short to ground with a meter
Clear the code and see if it returns right away
fix: Fix any shorted wiring first; if the wiring tests good, replace the pressure control solenoid "D".

checks: Inspect the wiring and ground connection for the pressure control solenoid "D" control circuit
Check for wires melted or rubbed together in the harness

Low, dirty or wrong transmission fluid
Wiring or connector with high resistance
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the pressure control solenoid "F" control circuit reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Find out whether the pressure control solenoid "F" itself or the system it works with is at fault, then repair or replace as needed.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid "F" Control Circuit Low
plain: The computer is watching the pressure control solenoid "F" control circuit and is reading a voltage that is lower than it should be, which often means a short to ground or a failed part. This solenoid inside the automatic transmission sets the fluid pressure that applies the clutches during shifts.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh, late or erratic shifts
Transmission may go into limp mode (stuck in one gear)

causes.name: Control wire to the pressure control solenoid "F" shorted to ground
Failed pressure control solenoid "F"
Corroded or loose connector
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the wiring in the pressure control solenoid "F" control circuit for rubbed-through insulation touching metal
Check the wiring for a short to ground with a meter
Clear the code and see if it returns right away
fix: Fix any shorted wiring first; if the wiring tests good, replace the pressure control solenoid "F".
